reason: The cited evidence shows that Al+Ti additions can form L12 precipitates in FCC HEAs (E1) and that coherent L12/B2 nanostructures can strengthen alloys (E2, E4), but none of the passages provide direct support for Al-induced short-range ordering as the nucleation mechanism, nor do they address radiation tolerance or oxidation resistance. The claims about defect sinks and cryogenic toughening are only loosely connected to the cited evidence, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: Increasing Al content in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni induces local chemical short-range ordering that nucleates coherent ordered nanoprecipitates (B2 or L12) in an FCC matrix.
These nanoprecipitates govern phase stability and simultaneously enhance high-temperature strength, oxidation resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Al-driven short-range ordering is the primary mechanism for nanoprecipitate formation, separable from other elemental effects.
Coherent ordered nanoprecipitates act as defect sinks, enhancing radiation tolerance.
Coherent ordered nanoprecipitates promote toughening mechanisms at cryogenic temperatures.
